deliveroo.source: Deliveroo_Master_Consolidation.xlsx — Weekly Summary. + ops from Weekly Summary sheet

issues: Covers fell by 169 (8.84%) week on week and spend per head rose by £0.11 (0.54%) to £20.20.
Sales were £37,600, down £1,857.27 (4.70%) week on week and £2,387.25 (5.97%) below target.
Labour was 24%.
Wet variance was 2.5% and food variance 0.6%.
Google reviews: 60 five star, 1 four star and 2 three star (one said the steak tataki was too salty, the other left no comment).
Deliveroo was busy on Saturday with some missing items and mistakes, so staff were reminded in the group chat to follow the proper processes.
No audit was done this week.
Staffing: a sushi chef is needed, and recruitment has started to cover Panma's holiday in November.
Extra staff were added for the half term week, when high revenue is expected, and for Saturday to pack and check Deliveroo orders.
Ziang Lin asked for BOH to be prepared on Friday nights for Saturday lunch service, with a minimum of six plus one staff instead of four plus one, and for the week's rota to be checked.
Maintenance: a high priority leak behind the cooker is logged, and someone was on site on 20/10 to fix the fuse for the pump.

Equipment: the induction hob arrived on 19/10 and the delivery station shelves are installed; a printer, a switch and Ethernet cables arrive this week and will be set up on a video call with Ziang Lin.

Student accommodation promotions should run once every four or five months per location to avoid repetition, and the site can run them itself if materials are stored properly on site, with Kai arranging everything.
Ziang Lin cannot visit on Saturday as he is heading back to Edinburgh; Ziang Lin or Kate will visit the week after next.
Upcoming: Slerp, Deliveroo, Halloween and half term.
Areas for improvement: quicker Deliveroo prep time, packing and checking orders, and cutting labour cost during the week.
Ziang Lin and Kaitlin Docherty plan to swap sites at the end of the month, with Ziang Lin working in Soho three days a week and Kaitlin Docherty covering Shoreditch and Southampton.

Region: the team aligned on implementing and keeping the dry ice presentation standard for volcano rolls and sashimi across sites: dry ice is poured at the table in a circular shape for volcano rolls, and sashimi is served on crushed ice in a red vegan ramen bowl with bamboo leaves and daikon to reduce dry ice waste.
Ziang Lin said Southampton would have beaten its sales target but for a Saturday downtime incident (AM Updates 21/10).

Southampton ran the region's first student accommodation B2B event, which generated 300 to 400 sign ups; the aim is at least four student events a month across South England, with £80 of materials stored on site so Diana can drive the van (AM Updates 21/10).
A fuse trip at the site needs follow up (Operations feedback meeting 21/10).
Region: Michael made rider wait time the priority delivery metric this week, followed by ratings; sites need a 4.7 Deliveroo rating to compete and open times above 99.5% (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: GMs and head chefs must run a daily morning brief for FOH and BOH using the app's daily tab to review sales, delivery ratings and setups (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: failed delivery orders come from items marked out of stock on Kobas but not on Deliverect, so managers must update both, snooze unavailable extras by PLU and check Deliverect failed order statuses daily (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: stock edit permissions will be suspended for one week to see true variances, after wastage and comps were used to bring variances under 5% and distort Kobas ordering baselines (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: from next week automated Gemini meeting recordings and dashboard sign offs replace manual meeting notes and KPI sheets, with tasks synced to Asana and the legacy spreadsheets kept as a backup for now (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: third party discounted bookings are no longer allowed on Saturdays and are capped at a share of capacity on other days (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: Hungry Panda still has untranslated menu text, wrong integrations and overridden PLUs; Sophie is to fix the setup, and Michael suggested turning it off if it hurts Deliveroo and Slerp without enough revenue (AM Updates 21/10).
